points: Keri M, a 50s marathoner, felt unwell during a race while on a GLP-1 drug.
She has completed dozens of half marathons and four full marathons previously.
The article raises questions about the safety of running marathons while on GLP-1 drugs.

summaries.summary: Woman discovers husband invited men to sexually assault her while she was sedated and restrained.
summaries.significance: The story highlights severe domestic abuse and betrayal, affecting the understanding of consent and trust within marriages.
points: Joanne Young's world was described as "tilted on its axis" upon discovery.
Philip Young, 50, advertised his wife on dating and swinging websites.
Four men are on trial for sexually assaulting Joanne while she was restrained and blindfolded.

summaries.summary: Oriel College faces calls to cancel an event with Nathan Cofnas, who accused Jason Arday of plagiarism.
points: Jason Arday, 41, resigned from Cambridge and was found dead in August.
Cofnas is scheduled to speak at Oriel College, supported by Reform UK student group.

summaries.summary: An article details setting up an offline coding agent using OpenCode, Ollama, and Qwen in a remote location with unreliable internet.
summaries.significance: This story matters as it demonstrates how developers can use offline AI agents for coding tasks in areas with unreliable internet, expanding remote work possibilities.
points: Uses Qwen3.5 9B model, weighing 6.6 GB, for local coding tasks.
Setup involves OpenCode for terminal interaction and Ollama for running Qwen locally.
Demonstrates offline coding capabilities, including explaining functions and refactoring code.

summaries.summary: Cynthia Erivo discusses her new film Prima Facie, where she plays a barrister who becomes a rape victim.
points: Erivo's character is a rising-star barrister defending men accused of sexual violence.
The film explores the impact on her character after being raped by a colleague.
Erivo mentions her disciplined lifestyle, including being vegan and running the London Marathon.

summaries.summary: Human rights activists urge Home Office to grant visa to former Weather Underground member for speaking on restorative justice.
summaries.significance: The story highlights the debate over granting entry to former radicals for educational purposes, influenced by cultural and legal figures.
points: Judith Clark, 77, invited by RSC to discuss restorative justice post-prison.
Home Office initially refused entry to Clark, a former radical group member.
Helena Kennedy, Harriet Walter, and Phyllida Lloyd advocate for visa reconsideration.

summaries.summary: Trump-appointed CDC deputy director Jennifer Shuford to resign after six months citing family reasons.
points: Jennifer Shuford appointed by Donald Trump in April.
Shuford cited desire to 'spend more time with my family' as resignation reason.
Resignation expected to occur after the midterm elections.

summaries.summary: UK government allocates £15m to a new anti-misogyny fund to combat sexism in various settings.
points: £15m fund targets misogyny in workplaces, schools, and public spaces.
Women and equalities minister Bridget Phillipson will lead the initiative.
Fund is the first national cash allocation to specifically address misogyny.

summaries.summary: Greens leader presses for human override in aged care assessment tool following a critical ombudsman report.
points: David Shoebridge urges legislative changes in the last two sitting weeks.
Ombudsman's 104-page report recommends allowing staff to correct algorithm decisions.
Report targets an "unfair" tool used for assessing home support packages for older Australians.
